6. Protecting SSH Keys with macOS Secure Enclave

Source: HackerNews | Topic: hn | Coverage: 1 source | Discussion

Summary

A new guide details how to integrate SSH keys with the macOS Secure Enclave for enhanced security. By offloading cryptographic operations to the hardware-backed Enclave, users can prevent private keys from being extracted from memory. This approach provides a significant security upgrade over standard software-based key storage.

My Take

Finally, a way to secure your SSH keys that doesn't involve hoping your laptop doesn't get stolen by someone who knows how to use a hex editor. It’s the digital equivalent of putting your house keys inside a vault that’s inside another vault. Just make sure you don't forget your password, or you’ll be locked out of your own servers until the heat death of the universe.
